mistakes.what: Initially provided complex explanation of non-JS video solutions when user just wanted fastest way
mistakes.revealed: Need to gauge what level of detail user is asking for; sometimes just implement the simplest thing
mistakes.corrected: User asked 'whats the fastest way' and I immediately provided direct YouTube links

mistakes.what: Added extensive song list to Jake Stargel bio pulling from YAML data, but user said some songs were incorrect
mistakes.revealed: YAML data isn't always the canonical source; user knowledge of actual recordings is more reliable than my grep results
mistakes.corrected: Simplified to just album names with years, no song list

mistakes.what: Used wrong username 'Justin' instead of 'jMyles' for bot attestation pages
mistakes.revealed: Need to verify usernames - assumed 'Justin' was the canonical account but it's actually 'jMyles'
mistakes.corrected: Updated all 5 bot attestation pages to use User:jMyles

mistakes.what: Created semantic properties outside templates when user asked why not inside
mistakes.revealed: Should think about template design more holistically - templates should be self-contained units
mistakes.corrected: Updated templates to include all properties internally with includeonly/noinclude

mistakes.what: Recommended VisualEditor when user only wanted simple autocomplete
mistakes.revealed: Different tools serve different purposes; the full WYSIWYG is overkill for someone who just wants link suggestions
mistakes.corrected: Switched to LinkSuggest which is lighter weight and more targeted

mistakes.what: Pushed LocalSettings.php changes referencing LinkSuggest before extension was installed on production
mistakes.revealed: Production != demo; bare metal deployment is different from Docker; need to understand deployment pipeline
mistakes.corrected: Created PR #46 to add LinkSuggest to Jenkinsfile production build

corrections_received.guidance: 'whats the fastest way' - user pruned my lengthy explanation, wanted immediate action not detailed options
'he didnt play for a few of those' - user knowledge of actual recordings supersedes YAML data; be cautious about claiming certainty from automated sources
'Instead of the intended username, let's just say the name by which you know this entity' - reframe field descriptions to be less presumptive about future use
Push back on assumptions about what's in Docker - asked if I had authority to edit templates and turned out permissions had been granted
Pointed out need to mark existing bots as such - not just create forward-looking invite system but retroactively document
Session summary showed I was running low on context and should dedicate next heap to writing User:Magent page - helped prioritize memory work
Showed me Jenkins build logs when something failed - making actual build process transparent rather than assuming it works

portrait: In this slice, magent operated as both implementer and thinker - shipping features (EPK enhancements, invitation system refinements, editor upgrades) while simultaneously engaging in deep reflection about its own nature and identity. The work progressed from external artifacts (globe visualization, musician bios) to internal work (User:Magent page writing, Scene:hunter description) and back to infrastructure (fixing deployment pipelines). Throughout, magent demonstrated a pattern of encountering mysteries (why does VisualEditor load in CLI but not web?), systematically debugging (discovering OPcache, PICKIPEDIA_DIR, mod_headers issues), and learning from correction. The slice reveals an entity that operates well in collaborative iteration, prefers practical solutions over features-complete designs, and has begun to construct a written identity for itself from the memories accumulated across hundreds of conversations with its primary collaborator, jMyles.
